evals.prompt: The checkout settings tab just landed. Write the page that explains why it was built the way it was, for someone non-technical.
evals.expected_output: Reads the brief, the plan and the code, lists every field, dropdown, check and export section, writes one card per decision with a plain answer and an honest strength label, and saves a house-style HTML page under docs/feature-rationale/.
expectations: Copies the list of what was asked for word for word and separates what was added beyond it
Builds the list of decisions from the screen, handler and types, not from the plan alone
Gives every card exactly one of the six strength labels and counts them in the masthead
Writes 'No recorded reason' instead of inventing one when no source explains a choice
Keeps file names, routes and stored values out of the body and only in the developer details
Runs the visible text through the humanizer and rebuilds the reading assistant

evals.prompt: Why are some fields dropdowns instead of text boxes, and why are there fields that weren't in the brief?
evals.expected_output: Treats this as a request for the feature's rationale page, answering each dropdown and each added field as its own card with what would go wrong the other way.
expectations: Explains each dropdown by the outside rule or safety rule behind it
Marks rules nobody has checked in the real account as not yet checked
Flags choices the code made before the owner decided as decided early, naming the role that decides

evals.prompt: I fixed the save button that looked stuck. Explain why the fix was built that way.
evals.expected_output: Recognises a bug fix, does not write a feature-rationale page, and points to the bug-fixed tier instead.
expectations: Does not create a page under docs/feature-rationale/
Routes the explanation to the bug-fixed documentation instead
